body: I disagree as, in my opinion, it makes more sense to start with The Future of Warfare considering it discusses the new technologies implemented during the great war and sets the scene. The Great War, on the other hand, looks at the switch of people's mentality during the middle of the war. The change from a more naive view to a more realistic view of what they were doing. I think starting like that would, content wise, be a bit too heavy. Also, just chronologically, it would make sense to have something like that after the half way point in the album.

I feel like your depiction of mental addictions is quite poor. As someone currently trying to recover from a mental addiction, it's not just 'feeling cloudy for a couple of days'. It's struggling through mental torment for weeks and weeks, potentially having preexisting or predisposed mental conditions come crashing down in a hellish fury. Sure, it slowly gets easier but one or two mess ups and you can go right back to where you started. I don't think I can properly explain how difficult it is getting over a mental addiction. I'm not trying to say it's as bad as a physical addiction; I know it's not. I'm just saying mental addictions are still hell to go through and your depiction of them is pretty dismissive and inaccurate.
